messages:
ara: Starting PHX networking bring-up thread — transit/BGP, NAT/egress sizing, and DNS delegation. Drafting a compact playbook, tagging folks: @mike for BGP, @irene for DNS/hosted zones, @sam for canary + oncall handoff.

mike: Ack. Couple of quick constraints: carrier requires private ASN 64512 for the peering, native BFD supported. We should plan for 2 BGP sessions (active/standby) and prefix filters to limit leaked routes.

ara: Good call. Notes for playbook: set local ASN to 64512, remote ASN per carrier (I'll paste after contract), set BFD timers to 50ms/3 for faster failover.

irene: DNS plan: create a customer private hosted zone phx.redwood.internal and delegate service records from core zone. We'll attach the zone to the PHX VPCs only. Need to add a conditional forwarder for the vendor-managed peering side for external mgmt FQDNs.

mike: Routing decisions: use TGW attachment for PHX and propagate routes only into the PHX route table. Do NOT enable auto-propagation into other regions. Use explicit route advertisements for the GPU subnets (10.40.0.0/18) and control-plane subnets (10.40.64.0/20). Tag route tables with "redwood:env=prod" and "redwood:role=phx-tgw" so infra scripts can pick them up.

sam: For NAT/egress: what's the plan — NAT GW per AZ or scaled NAT instances? We have heavy model download traffic during node boot.

ara: Tradeoffs: NAT Gateways are simpler but expensive at scale. For PHX initial stage (~16 GPU nodes) recommended: 1 NAT GW per AZ to avoid cross-AZ charges on heavy downloads, but configure an EIP pool and auto-swap via Lambda if we need to rotate. If we hit sustained egress > 8TB/month, move to NAT instances with autoscaling + iptables + connection tracking tuning.

mike: Add to playbook: create an EIP pool tagged redwood:phx-egress=true (5 EIPs) and a small route for ephemeral worker bootstrap that prefers NAT in the local AZ. Include health checks on NAT targets in Route53 health checks for quick failover.

irene: DNS delegation steps (brief): 1) Create phx.redwood.internal private hosted zone. 2) Add NS records in core.private.redwood.internal pointing to PHX name servers. 3) Attach zone to PHX VPCs. 4) Add split-horizon A records for internal registry + metadata service. 5) Add terraform snippet below:

irene: ```hcl
module "phx_private_zone" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/modules/route53//private-zone"
  zone_name = "phx.redwood.internal"
  vpc_ids = [module.phx_vpc.id]
  tags = {env = "prod" team = "infra"}
}
```

ara: Validation checklist for networking (smoke tests):
- BGP: verify established sessions on both peers via `show ip bgp summary`/cloud console.
- Routes: `tcptraceroute` from a jump host to a known external IP and to core services (10.10.0.5).
- DNS: resolve internal registry, ensure split-horizon behavior from inside/outside VPC.
- Egress: parallel download test from node to our object store to confirm no cross-AZ egress and measure throughput.
- KV cache connectivity for model-serving (port 6379) from worker nodes.
- Placeholder GPU nodes boot test: start 2 spot-style nodes and ensure they fetch model weights within 2m without failing connections.

mike: Add BGP validation commands in playbook: `aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments` and `show ip bgp neighbors` (for vendor) + `tcpdump -i any 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0'` on the peering router for SYN visibility.

sam: Oncall handoff template: environment, contact list, TGW attachment IDs, EIP pool ID, DNS zone ID, BGP remote ASN, expected prefixes. Include runbook link and escalation matrix. I can own the first 48h post-handoff.

ara: I'll assemble the final playbook and push to the infra runbooks repo under `networking/phx-2026-03`. Key items to include in the repo: terraform plan, one-click smoke script (`phx-network-smoke.sh`), monitoring dashboards (BGP session uptime, NAT bytes, DNS resolution latency), and cost estimate (NAT GW hourly x3 AZs + EIP transfer * projected 3 months).

irene: Cost note: Estimate ~ $1.2k/month for 3 NAT GWs (PHX egress patterns), plus EIP costs if we exceed 750 hours of static EIP. We'll include a forecast table in the PR.

mike: Security note: add route filters to prevent unintended advertisement of 10.0.0.0/8. Also lock down BGP to the exact prefixes we own.

ara: Action items assigned:
- mike: finalize BGP filters + vendor peering config (due EOD).
- irene: create private hosted zone and initial Terraform module (due tomorrow).
- sam: prepare oncall handoff doc & smoke runbook (due tomorrow).
- ara: create brief cost estimate and open PR for runbook (due EOD).

deploy-bot: smoke-deploy:phx-network-smoke.sh completed — all checks passed (BGP up, DNS resolving, egress test 600Mbps). :white_check_mark:

sam: Awesome — once PRs land I'll schedule the handoff and mark the cluster as `networking:green` in the rollout board.

ara: Thanks everyone. I'll post the runbook link when the PR is up and ping oncall. If we see any unexpected routing propagation, do not enable global propagation until further triage.

mike: FYI — I'll add a small mitigation: route leak detector that watches for unknown prefixes from the carrier and auto-blackholes the TGW attachment via Terraform apply pipeline.

ara: Perfect. Thread closed for now, will update with PR link.
